title: Letter 32 — Brief Counsels for the Path of Blessedness
attribution_note: Letter 32 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The path described in the holy Gospel

pairs.en: I received your letter through your father. I thank you that you remember me. Remember also what I said to you in brief.

I have noticed in your young heart a longing for the future blessedness. I wish that it may work in your heart and bring forth fruit. The path to that blessedness is not the path by which the Christians of this age walk, but the path described in the holy Gospel, which you have by you. Read it with reverence, attention and prayer, and it will show you the way, and taking you by the hand will lead you to that blessedness — only hearken to it. Yet I also offer you my counsel: attend to what I write.
1) Remember that you live in Petersburg, where as often as you go out of your lodging you see so much that leads away from the path of the pious. Guard yourself, then!
2) Remember: shun the corrupt as a plague. You will not soon discover on yourself the wound received from them, but it is far more harmful than the plague.
3) In every undertaking, deed and word, remember God. He notes all our deeds, words and thoughts, and writes them in His book, and renders to each according to his deeds.
4) When you lie down to sleep and when you rise from sleep, do not omit prayer.

5) Receive food and drink and the other goods with blessing and thanksgiving, and do not imitate those who behave as cattle: they eat and drink God's good and do not thank God. Such people are lost sheep, and go, with eyes shut, into eternal ruin.

6) Do not seek honour; but if it is given you, even beyond your strength, accept it, and do not rejoice in it, but hold it as a beast carries a pack laid upon it — a pack, I say, filled with something. Be in honour as a simple man, but do only what your honour and your oath require of you.
7) Deal kindly with every man, but have also a kind heart. For kind dealing without a kind heart is hypocrisy and craft. Guard against it!
8) Forgive injury and insult, and remember them not, and in the secret of your heart pray for him who inflicted them.

9) Always remember death, as an unknown summoner to the Lord. For we know not when our Lord will call us to Himself; and through death He calls every man to Himself. Remember also daily the judgment of God, torment and eternal life — and especially in the morning and when you lie down to sleep. This will not allow you to be corrupted.
10) Shun all luxury in food and clothing, as poison.
11) Shut your ears against rumours, and turn your eyes from looking on seductive faces, as from horrors.
12) Guard your tongue, and speak of no one except as need requires.
13) Finally, remember always that we shall leave all things here in the world, and go naked into that other world.
This brief counsel, yet useful to you, I send, and remain, wishing you the mercy of God,
